abstract: Blood cancers profoundly disrupt the bone marrow microenvironment, compromising its support for normal hematopoiesis. Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs), particularly Leptin receptor-high MSCs (LepRhigh-MSCs), are crucial niche components whose function is altered in diseases such as myeloid leukemia. Here, we employed single-cell multiomic RNA/ATAC-seq to comprehensively map changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility in MSCs from murine myeloid malignancy models. This unbiased analysis identified multiple regions of closed chromatin adjacent to niche-factor genes. Notably, we discovered a previously unrecognized enhancer downstream of Cxcl12, exclusively accessible in healthy LepRhigh-MSCs and regulated by the transcription factor Foxc1, whose expression is downregulated in LepRhigh-MSCs of myeloid malignancies. These results are consistent with a trend observed in deconvolved patient sequence data, and disruption of the enhancer impairs Cxcl12 expression for normal hematopoiesis. Collectively, these findings reveal a critical transcription factor-chromatin-mRNA regulatory axis that maintains hematopoietic niche integrity, highlighting a hidden regulatory vulnerability underlying blood cancers.
